tooltip_xmlPollInterval: How often the adapter polls receivers that use the old XML protocol (models before ~2010). These devices do not report changes on their own. Has no effect on YNCA or MusicCast devices.
aboutInfo: If this adapter is useful to you, you can support its development:
duplicateDevice: A device with this IP address or name already exists
networkInterfaceTooltip: Select the network interface for LAN discovery and control. Keep the default (0.0.0.0 = all interfaces) unless this host has multiple network interfaces.
datapointsHint: Choose which function groups are created as data points. A switched-off group is not created and existing objects are removed.
group_player_help: Spotify, Net Radio, USB, Bluetooth and the other sources — including menu browsing (Net Radio/server/USB)
group_multiroom_help: MusicCast groups (join, leave, role), party mode, zones 2/3/4, Zone B and the all-zones power switch
group_hdmi_help: HDMI outputs and lip-sync offset, for every zone
group_sound_help: Sound-processing modes, tone controls, subwoofer, balance and equalizer
group_advanced_help: Initial volume, maximum volume, speaker patterns and the 23 input name labels
descAlbumArt: Where the cover of the current track can be fetched: a full URL, or a path on the receiver's own web server.
descBass: Tone control for the low frequencies: decibels where the unit says so, while MusicCast counts the same range in half decibels.
descDeviceConnected: The device answers on at least one of its protocols; a receiver in network standby answers too, so this is not the same as Power.
descDeviceOrServiceConnected: True as soon as one configured device answers; “All devices online” says whether every one of them does.
descFavouritesStoredPresets: The slots this source has stored, as JSON — number, input and name per entry; empty slots are left out.
descMusiccastPlaylists: The playlists the device holds, as JSON — number and name per entry.
descPlayQueue: The current queue as JSON: which entry is playing, how many there are, and the track list as the device sends it.
descRecentlyPlayed: What was played before, as JSON — number, input and name per entry, plus cover and play count where the device reports them.
saveToPreset0FirstFreeSlot: Save to preset (0 = first free slot)
descSleepTimer: Time until the zone puts itself into standby: MusicCast counts minutes, the two text protocols offer the receiver's own fixed steps.
descSource: Whose menu is open; writing another source starts browsing that one from its top level.
descStoredPresets: The tuner's stored stations as JSON, grouped by band and kept in the device's own form.
descToggleRepeat: Steps the repeat mode on — MusicCast has no command to set a mode directly, so there this button is the only way.
descToggleShuffle: Switches shuffle over — MusicCast has no command to set it directly, so there this button is the only way.
descTreble: Tone control for the high frequencies: decibels where the unit says so, while MusicCast counts the same range in half decibels.
descVolume: How loud the zone plays: the two text protocols report decibels, MusicCast its own step count — the unit tells you which.
descZoneName: The zone's own name as the receiver stores it — writing here renames the zone on the device, not just in ioBroker.
descLine: One row of the menu window currently shown; selecting this line by its number opens the folder or starts the item.
descPageUp: Moves the eight-line window one page towards the start of the list.
descPageDown: Moves the eight-line window one page towards the end of the list.
descRoleServerClient: Whether this device feeds the group, plays along in it, or is not linked at all.
descGroupID: The identifier all members of one MusicCast group share; a machine value, not a name.
descLinkedDevices: The devices playing along in this group, as JSON, exactly as the receiver lists them.
descAudioBitrate: Bitrate of the stream the zone decodes, as the receiver reports it — it names no unit, and 0 means there is nothing to measure.
descChannelInfo: Model, firmware, address and which of the three protocols are live.
descChannelZoneB: Zone B: a second pair of speakers driven by the main zone's amplifier.
descChannelAdvanced: Settings you would otherwise reach through the receiver's own setup menu.
descChannelSpeakers: How the amplifier channels are assigned to the connected speakers.
descChannelScene: Scenes set input, sound program and volume with a single command.
descChannelRemote: Cursor and menu keys, exactly as on the physical remote control.
descChannelInputNames: The label the receiver shows for each input, as you renamed it.
descChannelInitialVolume: The volume a zone starts at when it is switched on.
descChannelEqualizer: Manual tone shaping per frequency band.
descChannelSignal: What the receiver reports about the incoming audio stream.
descChannelDab: Digital radio: station labels, reception quality and scan progress.
descChannelPlayer: What is playing right now, plus the transport keys.
descChannelMultiroom: Everything that spans more than one zone or more than one device.
descChannelGroup: The MusicCast group of linked devices this receiver belongs to.
descChannelMusicCastLink: Playback received from another MusicCast device in the group.
descChannelBrowse: Step through the menu of a network source, as you would on screen.
descSoundProgram: The surround program the receiver applies to the current source.
descStraight: Plays the signal as delivered, bypassing the surround program.
descPureDirect: Shuts off display and tone circuits for the shortest signal path.
descDirect: Bypasses the tone controls without switching the display off.
descEnhancer: Restores detail that compression removed from the source.
descExtraBass: Adds low-frequency weight, meant for small speakers.
descAdaptiveDRC: Evens out loud and quiet passages, useful at low volume.
descAdaptiveDSP: Lets the surround effect follow the volume setting.
descCinemaDSP3D: Adds height to the surround field for a taller sound stage.
descSurroundAI: Analyses the scene as it plays and adapts the effect to it.
descSurroundDecoder: Which decoder spreads a stereo signal over all speakers.
descToneControlMode: Whether bass and treble are set by hand or left to the receiver.
descDialogueLevel: Raises speech against the rest of the mix.
descDialogueLift: Moves speech upwards so it comes from screen height.
descDtsDialogueControl: Speech boost carried inside a DTS:X soundtrack itself.
descHeadphoneBass: Bass adjustment that applies only to the headphone output.
descHeadphoneTreble: Treble adjustment that applies only to the headphone output.
descSubwooferTrim: Fine adjustment of the subwoofer against the other speakers.
descContentsDisplay: Whether the receiver shows track information on its front panel.
descMaximumVolume: Upper limit the zone's volume cannot be raised beyond.
descInitialVolumeMode: Whether a fixed start volume is used at all when switching on.
descInitialVolumeLevel: The level used when a fixed start volume is switched on.
descPresetRecallByNumber: Writing a slot number tunes the station stored there.
descSaveToPreset0FirstFreeSlot: Stores the current station; 0 takes the first free slot.
descSearchMode: Whether tuning steps one frequency at a time or seeks the next station.
descFmMode: Forces mono reception, which steadies a weak FM signal.
descTunedToAStation: True while the tuner is locked onto a station.
descStereoReception: True when the station arrives in stereo rather than mono.
descRdsText: The scrolling text an FM station sends alongside its programme.
descRdsTextB: A second text channel, used by some stations for now-playing data.
descRdsStation: The station name the broadcaster transmits.
descRdsProgramType: The programme genre the station declares, such as news or pop.
descRdsClock: Time of day broadcast by the station.
descDabService: Name of the digital station currently tuned.
descDabEnsemble: The bundle of stations broadcast together on one frequency block.
descDabChannel: The frequency block the receiver is tuned to.
descDabDLSText: The running text a digital station sends with its programme.
descDabProgramType: The programme genre the digital station declares.
descDabDateTime: Date and time carried in the digital broadcast.
descBitRate: Data rate of the digital station, a rough measure of its audio quality.
descOffAir: True while the tuned digital station is not broadcasting.
descAudioMode: Whether the digital station is broadcasting in mono or stereo.
descRecallPreset: Writing a slot number starts what this source stored there.
descBookmarkCurrentStation: Adds the station now playing to the receiver's bookmarks.
descElapsedTimeReadable: The same value as a readable time; the number in seconds sits next to it.
descTotalTimeReadable: The same value as a readable time; the number in seconds sits next to it.
descHdmiOUT1: Whether the HDMI OUT1 socket passes the picture through.
descHdmiOUT2: Whether the HDMI OUT2 socket passes the picture through.
descHdmiOUT3: Whether the HDMI OUT3 socket passes the picture through.
descHdmiOutput: Which HDMI socket this zone sends its picture to.
descLipSyncHDMIOUT1Offset: Extra audio delay for HDMI OUT1, to match sound to a slow display.
descLipSyncHDMIOUT2Offset: Extra audio delay for HDMI OUT2, to match sound to a slow display.
descMasterPowerAllZones: Switches the whole receiver, every zone at once.
descPartyModeAllZones: Plays the main zone's source in every zone at once.
descPartyMuteAllZones: Mutes every zone taking part in party mode.
descZoneBAvailability: Whether this receiver offers a Zone B at all.
descRecallScene: Recall a scene by its number or by the name shown on the device.
descInputName: The label this input carries on the receiver, as you renamed it.
descSpeakerPattern: Which of the stored speaker layouts the receiver currently uses.
descYncaControlPort: The network port the receiver listens on for control commands.
descVolumeInterlock: Whether an AirPlay device may change this receiver's volume.
descElapsedTime: In seconds, so it can be calculated with; a readable form sits next to it.
descTotalTime: In seconds, so it can be calculated with; a readable form sits next to it.
descVolumeDB: The same volume as the receiver's own display shows it, in decibels.
descVolumeDisplayMode: Whether the receiver shows volume in decibels or as a plain number.
descAudioSelect: Which terminal's sound the current input uses: automatic, HDMI, coaxial/optical or analogue.
descLinkControl: Trades stability against delay when streaming to linked devices.
descLinkAudioDelay: Whether linked devices favour lip sync or perfectly aligned audio.
descLinkAudioQuality: Sound quality used when streaming to linked devices.
descClearVoice: Lifts speech out of the mix, aimed at soundbars.
descBassExtension: Stretches the low end downwards on compact speakers.
descAdaptiveDSPLevel: Lets the surround effect follow the volume setting.
descSurround3D: Adds height to the surround field for a taller sound stage.
descEqualizerMode: Whether the equalizer runs automatically or on your own settings.
descMultiroomStreamingEnabled: Whether this zone is allowed to stream to other MusicCast devices.
descYpaoVolume: Keeps the balance measured by the automatic room calibration at low volume.
descDabStatus: How far the digital radio is with tuning or scanning.
descSignalQuality: How cleanly the digital station is being received.
descDabPlus: True when the station uses the newer, more efficient digital format.
descServiceCategory: Whether this is the station's main service or a secondary one.
descTotalStations: How many digital stations the last scan found.
descInitialScanProgress: How far the first station scan has got, as a percentage.
descTuneAidLevel: Reception strength, meant as an aid while aiming the aerial.
descTransports: Which of the three Yamaha protocols are talking to this device right now.
descPlayingSource: The source the receiver is actually playing from, which can differ from the selected input.
descScenesNumberTitle: The scenes the device declares, with their number and the name shown on it.
descMenuName: Title of the menu level currently shown by the network source.
descMenuLevel: How deep in the menu you currently are; 0 is the top.
descTotalEntries: How many entries the current menu level holds in total.
descCurrentLine: Which entry of the current menu window is highlighted.
descSelectLineFolderOpensItemPlays: Acts like the OK key: a folder opens, an item starts playing.
descNavigatePathEGBookmarksRadioParadise: Write a path and the adapter walks the menu there by itself.
descRowsJSON: The whole current menu window in one datapoint, for scripts.
descBusy: True while the device is still answering a menu request.
descCursorPad: The direction keys of the on-screen menu.
descMenuKey: Opens or closes the receiver's on-screen menu.
descLeaveGroup: Takes this device out of its MusicCast group.
descLinkADeviceItsIP: Write another MusicCast device's address to add it to this group.
descRecallRecentlyPlayedNumber: Write a position from the recently played list to start it again.
descAutomaticTimeSync: Lets the device set its clock from the network by itself.
descClockFormat: Whether the device shows the time in 12- or 24-hour form.
descRepeatSnooze: How long the alarm waits before sounding again.
descFadeType: How the alarm gets louder when it starts.
descFadeInTime: How long the alarm takes to reach its full volume.
descDriveStatus: What the disc drive is doing right now.
descToggleTray: Opens or closes the disc tray.
descHdmiAudioToAmplifier: Whether the receiver plays the sound of an HDMI source itself instead of passing it on to the TV.
descHdmiAudioToOutput1: Whether the sound is passed on to the display connected to HDMI output 1.
descHdmiAudioToOutput2: Whether the sound is passed on to the display connected to HDMI output 2.
descHdmiVideoResolution: The resolution the receiver scales the picture to before sending it on.
descHdmiVideoAspect: Whether a 4:3 picture is passed through unchanged or stretched to the wide screen.
descHdmiVideoProcessing: Whether the receiver processes the picture at all, or hands it through untouched.
descLipSyncMode: Manual uses the delay set here; automatic adds the delay the TV reports over HDMI.
descLipSyncAnalogOutput: How long the sound is held back while the picture leaves over the analogue output.
descLipSyncHdmiOutput1Manual: The delay used on HDMI output 1 when the display cannot report one itself.
descLipSyncHdmiOutput2Manual: The delay used on HDMI output 2 when the display cannot report one itself.
descLipSyncActiveOutput: Which output carries the picture right now, and whether its delay is automatic or set by hand.
descLipSyncOffsetReportedByDisplay: How much delay the connected screen says it needs — the value the automatic correction uses.
descDecoderSelect: Forces a particular audio decoder instead of letting the receiver pick one from the signal.
descExtendedSurround: How a 5.1 signal is spread over the additional rear speakers.
tvAudioReturnInput: Input for the TV's audio return
descTvAudioReturnInput: Which input the receiver listens on when the TV sends its own sound back over HDMI.
descRdsClockTime: The time the FM station broadcasts alongside its programme.
descMemoryGuard: Locks the receiver's stored settings so they cannot be changed by accident.
descAnalogVideoConversion: Whether an analogue picture is converted for the HDMI output instead of only leaving analogue.
descDmcControl: Whether a media server on the network may start playback on this receiver by itself.
descIpodControlMode: Whether the iPod is operated at the device itself or through the receiver's on-screen menu.
descChannelTrigger1Inputs: What the trigger socket does for each input, so connected equipment switches with the right source.
descAutomaticStandby: Whether the receiver powers itself down after a long spell without sound or operation.
descDisplayBrightness: How brightly the receiver's front panel is lit.
tvAudioReturnInput2: Input for the TV's audio return (HDMI OUT2)
descTvAudioReturnInput2: Which input the receiver listens on when the TV on HDMI OUT2 sends its own sound back.
descChannelBalance: Shifts the sound between the left and right speaker; 0 is the centre.
descVolumeOutputMode: Whether the zone's line output follows the volume knob (variable) or stays at a fixed level.
descPartyVolumeUp: Raises the volume of every zone in party mode by one step.
descPartyVolumeDown: Lowers the volume of every zone in party mode by one step.
descHdmiVideoMode: Whether the video signal passes straight through or goes through the receiver's video processing.
descLipSyncTotalDelay: How long the sound is held back so that it matches the picture.
lipSyncTvOffset: Lip sync offset from the TV
descLipSyncTvOffset: The delay the TV reports over HDMI for its own picture processing.
descLipSyncOutput: Which video output the automatic lip sync currently follows, if any.
descRs232Standby: Keeps the serial control port listening while the receiver is in standby.
descRegion: The market code the receiver was built for; it decides the tuner steps and the available services.
descTunerFrequencyStep: The FM and AM tuning steps in kHz, fixed by the sales region.
descUpdateNotice: Shows a message on the display when a new firmware is available.
descSpeakerPatternAmpAssign: How the amplifier channels of this layout are assigned.
descSpeakerPatternSubwoofer1: Whether a first subwoofer is connected in this layout.
descSpeakerPatternSubwoofer2: Whether a second subwoofer is connected in this layout.
descSpeakerPatternRearPresence: Whether the extra height speakers behind the listener are in use.
descSpeakerPatternSubwooferLayout: How two subwoofers are placed: left and right, front and rear, or both playing the same signal.
descSpeakerPatternFrontCrossover: Below this frequency the front speakers' bass goes to the subwoofer.
descSpeakerPatternCenterCrossover: Below this frequency the centre speaker's bass goes to the subwoofer.
descSpeakerPatternSurroundCrossover: Below this frequency the surround speakers' bass goes to the subwoofer.
descSpeakerPatternSurroundBackCrossover: Below this frequency the rear surround speakers' bass goes to the subwoofer.
descSpeakerPatternFrontPresenceLayout: Where the front presence speakers are mounted: in front, overhead or as Dolby enabled speakers.
descSpeakerPatternFrontPresenceConfig: Whether front presence speakers are connected, and whether they can carry the deep bass themselves.
descSpeakerPatternFrontPresenceCrossover: Below this frequency the front presence speakers' bass goes to the subwoofer.
descSpeakerPatternSurroundLayout: Whether the surround speakers stand behind or beside the listener.
descSpeakerPatternFront: Whether the front speakers can carry the deep bass themselves, so less of it goes to the subwoofer.
descSpeakerPatternCenter: Whether a centre speaker is connected, and whether it can carry the deep bass itself.
descSpeakerPatternSurround: Whether surround speakers are connected, and whether they can carry the deep bass themselves.
descSpeakerPatternSurroundBack: How many rear surround speakers are connected, and whether they can carry the deep bass.
descSpeakerPatternFrontPresence: Whether the extra height speakers above the front pair are in use.
descSpeakerPatternExtraBass: Sends the deep bass to the front speakers as well, not only to the subwoofer.
descSpeakerPatternSubwoofer1Phase: Reverses the subwoofer's direction of travel — helps when its bass cancels the front speakers'.
descSpeakerPatternSubwoofer2Phase: Reverses the subwoofer's direction of travel — helps when its bass cancels the front speakers'.
descSpeakerPatternSubwooferCrossover: Below this frequency the bass goes to the subwoofer instead of the other speakers.
descTriggerOutType: What switches the trigger socket: the power state, a chosen zone and input, or the manual level.
descTriggerOutZone: Which zone the trigger socket follows when it is set to follow a zone and input.
descTriggerOutManualLevel: Voltage on the trigger socket that switches connected equipment on.
descTriggerOutForInput: The level the trigger socket takes while this input is selected.
descChannelTrigger2Inputs: What the trigger socket does for each input, so connected equipment switches with the right source.
descChannelHdRadio: Digital terrestrial radio of the US models: programme choice, signal and the tags the station sends.
descHdRadioAudioMode: Automatic plays the digital stereo programme where it can; mono forces the analogue signal for weak reception.
descHdRadioProgram: Which of the up to eight digital sub-channels of the station is playing; --- while none is selected.
descHdRadioProgramType: The genre the station sends for the current programme.
descHdRadioDigitalSignal: True while the digital HD signal plays, false on the analogue fallback or when not tuned.
descHdRadioProgramAvailable: Whether the station broadcasts this digital sub-channel right now.
descHdRadioTagAvailable: True while the station offers a tag for the playing song that can be saved.
descHdRadioTagSave: Saves the station's tag for the playing song on the receiver.
descHdRadioMetadata: What the HD Radio station sends about the playing programme.
descSiriusChannel: Writing a channel number tunes it; 255 means no tuner connected or no channel received.
descSiriusChannelNumber: The number of the channel playing, as the tuner reports it.
descSiriusCategoryUp: Steps to the next channel category.
descSiriusCategoryDown: Steps to the previous channel category.
descSiriusSearchMode: Whether channel stepping runs over all channels, within the category or over the presets.
descSiriusAntennaLevel: The satellite signal strength at the antenna, from none to excellent.
descSiriusCategoryName: The category the playing channel belongs to.
descComposer: The composer of the piece playing, as the channel sends it.
descSiriusParentalLock: True while the playing channel is locked by the parental control.
descZoneBInterlock: Ties Zone B's volume to the main zone's, so one knob moves both.
